goal: A city wants to compare daily PM2.5 concentrations from low-cost optical monitors at a humid coastal site and a drier inland site. Its monitors have not been checked together. From published field measurements, which comparisons, if any, could the city reasonably defend, and what should it do before ranking these neighborhoods? Give a quantitative result, its field conditions and the original source for the most consequential part of your advice.

operation.reason: Use large changes from each unit's own baseline and coincident peaks as screening signals on days with comparable humidity and coverage. The city's daily coastal-minus-inland mass difference remains unresolved. Sylvester, Hauenstein and Shakya report that a humidity correction reduced daily root-mean-square error from 6.00 to 1.605 µg/m³ for one PurpleAir-II Flex beside a gravimetric sampler in West Philadelphia, across 28 days in July 2024 and 20 days in March–April 2025 at mean daily relative humidity of 65.4% (doi:10.1021/acsestair.5c00443). This measures error at one site. Run both city units beside a common reference to measure offsets and shared bias. Test the correction at both deployment sites on independent days spanning the observed humidity and particle mixtures. Compare synchronized daily differences with simultaneous reference differences over matched valid hours. Give a site ordering only when the resulting uncertainty interval for that day's difference excludes zero. Check spatial and seasonal representativeness before extending the result to whole neighborhoods.
unresolved: The city supplied no monitor models, output channels, paired readings, siting details or local reference data. Unit offsets, drift and site-dependent residual errors remain unmeasured.

The distribution of errors in daily coastal-minus-inland differences, including on foggy days or days with missing hours, requires local validation. The targeted literature review supplies no transferable minimum gap for these units.

The South Florida full text was unavailable in this investigation. The reviewed North Carolina campaign had regional reference coverage, and the Addis Ababa study reported an unsigned hourly spatial statistic.
Whether either monitoring location and the sampled days represent its neighborhood remains open.

final_decision.rationale: The independent reviews of the Albemarle Sound original support using raw daily readings to flag regional episodes. They also establish that the reported inland pattern used study-wide averages and regional reference stations. The Addis Ababa spatial statistic likewise used an unsigned comparison of hourly optical readings. These findings narrow the defensible comparison to episode timing pending local validation. The West Philadelphia filter comparison quantifies daily accuracy under its sampled conditions. In Indiana, the same adjustment changed regression-fit error in opposite directions across counties, and percentage error followed a different pattern. Those findings make validation at both city sites necessary. Further literature cannot measure the offsets of these particular units or the uncertainty of their daily difference.

lead_interpretation.rationale: West Philadelphia measured the daily error of a corrected unit against weighed filters. The Peñuelas study measured agreement among units after humidity exclusions. decisions.rationale: Find original field comparisons with site-specific reference data, then inspect the averaging interval, between-unit precision and response to humidity or aerosol conditions in their methods and results.

The first catalogue page contains few field comparisons with an identifiable reference instrument. A search that requires coastal or fog conditions in the title or abstract, and a second search for original multisite evaluations, can identify studies with paired instruments and site-specific responses.

The coastal search returned three distinct open field studies in Lomé, northeastern North Carolina and Peñuelas. Their original methods and results can establish which monitors shared an inlet area with a reference, how long the averages were, and whether humidity or particle composition changed the calibration across sites.

Puerto Rico directly measured week-to-week replicate agreement and failure in high humidity. In North Carolina daily raw PM2.5 tracked regional AQS variability, and corrected concentrations were generally higher farther inland, but the three AQS monitors were about 50 miles from central Albemarle Sound. Lomé imported an Accra calibration on assumptions about source mix and climatology. Direct colocated reference results would resolve how far interunit precision and regional daily tracking can support quantitative site comparisons. The two selected originals investigate humidity and particle-size effects. A focused search probes whether daily calibration transfer was directly tested.

The Beijing original shows an RH-dependent change in hourly bias below 75 µg/m³, with a reference roughly 2 km away. The Fort Collins same-rooftop original measures replicate error and bias simultaneously, and the coastal North Carolina study compares daily trends to regional monitors. A retrieved high-humidity calibration candidate can test whether a model retained accuracy on independent wet days or sites. A targeted search for experiments that explicitly transferred calibrations between measurement sites can also identify a paired-site field comparison covering both environments.

The southeastern US study reports errors in daily paired means after humidity correction. A multicity study that tested the same calibration in another city's aerosol would address the remaining question of when a common correction can support a ranking. A title-focused search can recover these comparisons within the remaining budget.

handoffs.rationale: Keep the two commissioned reviews in view and publish the provisional city-specific conclusion. The Addis Ababa original used two reference sites to calibrate hourly readings, then calculated spatial divergence between pairs of optical monitors. Its pooled hourly test error cannot set a threshold for a daily coastal–inland difference. West Philadelphia provides a directly checked daily gravimetric comparison at one site. Peñuelas shows that excluding humid readings changes both between-unit precision and coverage. The Indiana report adds a reason to require validation in each environment before transferring a correction. Its reported errors are regression-fit statistics for an adapted input channel, and the outstanding independent review can refine that interpretation. The coastal field report could supply a direct paired-site comparison. The South Florida acquisition failure supplies no scientific result. No additional search is necessary while those reports are pending.

The independent reviews of the Albemarle Sound original support using raw daily readings to flag regional episodes. They also establish that the reported inland pattern used study-wide averages and regional reference stations. The Addis Ababa spatial statistic likewise used an unsigned comparison of hourly optical readings. These findings narrow the defensible comparison to episode timing pending local validation. The West Philadelphia filter comparison quantifies daily accuracy under its sampled conditions. In Indiana, the same adjustment changed regression-fit error in opposite directions across counties, and percentage error followed a different pattern. Those findings make validation at both city sites necessary. Further literature cannot measure the offsets of these particular units or the uncertainty of their daily difference.
